lines.desc: Surface water - attenuation, swales, filter drains, outfalls, flow control
lines.basis: RE-PRICED 18 Aug 2026 (second pass) AGAINST THE ACTUAL REPORT, AND THIS CORRECTS THE FIRST PASS. Earlier today this line was raised to GBP 1,250,000 on the reading that the Environment Agency had ruled infiltration drainage out. The RAB Consultants Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy of September 2023, now in Research/planning-file, says the opposite for this site: 'The site is shown to lie on a superficial geology of sand and gravel with a soil consistency of freely draining loamy soils', and the designed scheme uses permeable pavement and a cellular storage tank with a working infiltration coefficient. Groundwater was encountered at 2.51 m below ground rising to 2.30 m, so the tank sits 1 m above it. The Source Protection Zone constraint is real but applies to contaminated runoff, not clean roof water. WHAT REMAINS TRUE: that FRA covers 0.414 ha of hardstanding for a fifteen-bedroom ancillary scheme. Sixty keys, twelve houses, a spa building, an eighty-bed village and the river works are many times that area, and the greenfield discharge rate the design is held to (QBAR 0.2 l/s) does not scale. Set at GBP 1,050,000: above the original GBP 890,000 because the area is far larger, below GBP 1,250,000 because infiltration is available where the runoff is clean.

lines.desc: Flood mitigation - riverside and Meadows only, flood-resilient construction
lines.basis: RE-SCOPED AND REDUCED 18 Aug 2026 on primary evidence. The whole budget has carried a Flood Zone 3 basis with finished floor levels raised to 33.22 mAOD, taken from a February 2021 RAB report quoted second-hand in the John Simpson design statement - the report itself was never in the data room. The RAB Flood Risk Assessment of September 2023, submitted with 23/07589/FUL and now in Research/planning-file, states plainly and repeatedly: 'the site lies in Flood Zone 1, which is described in the NPPF as land having a less than 1 in 1,000 annual probability of river or sea flooding (less than 0.1% AEP)', and 'The site is approximately 350m from the River Thames'. It further records that the site and its access do not flood in the 3.33% or 1% AEP events. THE COURTYARD BUILDINGS ARE NOT IN THE FLOODPLAIN. What is: the River Club building on the Thames bank, the Long Water works, and the Meadows residential ground in the south of the estate, which Savills places at the river. This line is therefore re-scoped to those, and cut from GBP 520,000 to GBP 280,000. Note the River Club building already carries its own raised-construction premium in zone 10. Also note the two RAB reports disagree, and only the 2023 one has been read in the original.

lines.desc: Ground investigation and contamination remediation allowance
lines.basis: HELD AT GBP 950,000 on 18 Aug 2026 and re-based on the primary report. The Opus Joynes Pike contamination assessment is now in Research/planning-file and it is a PHASE 1 DESK STUDY DATED 11 SEPTEMBER 2009. It records: at least ten above-ground oil storage tanks, most of the older metal ones with no secondary containment and 'considered unlikely to comply with requirements of the Control of Pollution (Oil Storage) (England) Regulations 2001'; hydrocarbon odour in the house basement and oil staining on the boiler room floor; a garage workshop with oils, greases, asbestos from brake linings, acids from batteries, solvents and pesticides; a historic gasometer just beyond the boundary; and the disposal of untreated sewage from the cess pits to land, which it recommends 'is stopped immediately as this is considered to be an illegal activity'. The site is a MAJOR AQUIFER in GROUNDWATER SOURCE PROTECTION ZONE III with soils of 'intermediate to high leaching potential', and eight groundwater abstractions within 250 m. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: the report recommends 'a Phase 2 intrusive investigation is carried out to identify whether relevant pollutant linkages exist' - trial pits, window sampling, gas and groundwater monitoring wells. NO PHASE 2 INVESTIGATION EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE 147 DOCUMENTS ON THE PUBLIC REGISTER. Seventeen years after the desk study told the owner to quantify the liability, nobody has. Condition 11 of 23/07589/FUL makes remediation a pre-commencement gate. GBP 950,000 is an allowance against an unquantified liability, and a Phase 2 investigation is the first thing a buyer should commission.

lines.desc: Long Water - isolation sluice, water treatment, regeneration zones, steps and changing
lines.basis: The Long Water becomes an isolated, treated outdoor swimming water. ISOLATION IS NOT OPTIONAL. River Action and the Henley and Marlow group test this reach intensively each year before the Regatta: almost half of 27 tests in May and June failed bathing standards, and levels reached 25,000 E. coli per 100ml on 19 June - 27 times the threshold the Environment Agency grades as poor. The testing is carried out near Fawley Meadows, where the effluent from the Henley sewage treatment works enters the river; that is the estate's southern boundary. Thames-connected water at Fawley cannot be marketed for swimming. The operating template is Canary Wharf's Eden Dock - lifeguarded sessions, a partner operator and published testing - but the mechanism does not transfer, because that dock is spring-fed from an aquifer through Thanet sand and gravel. Scope here is a sluice isolating the canal from the river, regenerative filtration with planted zones, bank steps and a changing and drying point. RULED AT GBP 1.5m LOADED IN TOTAL (18 Aug 2026), of which the 420 m of bank strengthening carries GBP 868k on its own line, leaving GBP 632k here. That is thin for a sluice and a treated swimming body, and it is a ruled budget rather than a costed scope. Altering a Capability Brown water feature inside a Grade II* registered park is a heritage consent in its own right.

Allowance, not an assessment - no licence application has been made and the 2023 survey post-dates none of our scheme.
